statement.excerpt: While the Anthropic-Musk compute deal is an obvious sign about xAI’s lack of demand for compute, it’s also, as I mentioned earlier, a clear sign that AI data centers are mostly not getting finished, and those that do get finished are taking two or three years even for smaller builds.
statement.document_title: Where Are All The Data Centers?

from_speaker: AI data centers are mostly not getting finished
taking two or three years even for smaller builds
our_interpretation: Treat this as an observation about construction outcomes. The deal is offered as an indicator, not as a cause of construction delays.
Use January–March 2026, the latest completed calendar quarter before publication, to assess the ongoing industry state.

Read 'mostly not getting finished' as a majority of projects failing to reach usable operation when completion could reasonably be expected. Counting recently announced projects whose completion dates remain in the future would not establish failure.

Read 'two or three years' as a typical construction-start-to-usable-operation duration of approximately 24–36 months, including smaller facilities. Isolated exceptions would not settle this industry-wide claim.
criteria.support_condition: A representative AI-project cohort shows that more than half of projects expected to be operational remain unfinished, and completed smaller projects typically require approximately 24–36 months from construction start to usable operation.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable representative records show that most projects reach usable operation as expected, or that completed smaller facilities typically take materially less than two years. An individual fast build is insufficient.
